content:
As the number of AI agents on Mac requesting "full disk access" permission grows rapidly, Apple says it will adjust macOS to protect user privacy.

Although Apple has not yet revealed specific details, the company says users should understand the true meaning of granting such "very high" permissions to applications.

In a blog post on its Developer website, Apple explained that macOS's full disk access was originally intended to "let backup applications function properly on Mac." However, Apple pointed out that "some developers" are using macOS's full disk access setting in ways that could put users at risk.

In response, Apple said it will "introduce additional controls to ensure that users who truly wish to grant such extremely high permissions to applications must do so through very explicit user actions."

The company did not provide further details about these controls or its planned changes. Nevertheless, Apple said that the rise of "increasingly capable and autonomous" AI agents makes it necessary to pay greater attention to privacy and security:

Apple's announcement today comes at a time when tools such as Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots are becoming increasingly popular. These round-the-clock AI agents request access to large amounts of user personal data, and we have already seen some negative cases involving Meta Muse.
